n: Paul’s third visit is coming. He cites the law’s principle that every charge must be confirmed by two or three witnesses — he will deal with matters fairly.

f.w: In the mouth of two or three witnesses

n: He warned them on his second visit and warns again now: when he comes, he won’t spare those who continue in sin.
They wanted proof that Christ speaks through Paul. Christ isn’t weak toward them, but powerful among them.

f.w: a proof of Christ speaking in me

n: Christ was crucified in weakness, yet lives by God’s power. Likewise the apostles are weak in Him but will live with Him by God’s power in dealing with them.

f.w: liveth by the power of God

n: Rather than testing Paul, they should test themselves: are they living in the faith? Don’t they realize Christ is in them — unless they fail the test?

f.g: Those who fail the test, disqualified.

n: Paul trusts they’ll see that he hasn’t failed the test.
He prays they will do no wrong — not so he looks good, but so they do what is right, even if he seems to have failed.
The apostles can’t act against the truth, only for it.
He is glad to be weak if they are strong. What he prays for is their full restoration and maturity.

f.g: Being fully restored, mended, made complete.

n: He writes now so that when he comes, he won’t have to be harsh in using the authority the Lord gave him to build up, not tear down.

f.w: to edification, and not to destruction

n: His farewell: rejoice, aim for wholeness, take comfort, be united, live in peace — and the God of love and peace will be with them.

f.g: Be made complete, set things right.

n: Greet one another with a holy kiss of affection.
All the saints with Paul send their greetings.

f.g: The believers in Macedonia, where Paul was writing.

n: Paul closes with a blessing naming all three members of the Godhead: the grace of Christ, the love of God the Father, and the fellowship of the Holy Ghost.

f.w: the communion of the Holy Ghost
f.g: Fellowship and sharing that the Holy Ghost creates.
